method: isolated Q4 GEMV microbench: Hot banks uploaded once, 200 iters, dispatch+sync only (NOT gemv_quant_host which re-uploads each call)
note: measured under GPU contention from a concurrent session; relative ratios robust, absolute GB/s mildly depressed
finding: OLD one-thread-per-row Q4 GEMV already runs at 170-277 GB/s = 62-100% of peak. New MLX simd kernel is only 1.03-1.5x (near-noise on several shapes), NOT the 2-4x docs/bottleneck.md projected. Kernels are near roofline.
bottleneck_doc_error: The '~6-20% of bandwidth / ~4x on the table' claim came from the gemv_quant_host microbench which re-uploads 4.9MB/call, measuring UPLOAD bandwidth not kernel bandwidth.
roofline: E4B 21.5 tok/s = 46.5ms/tok; weight traffic ~2.86GB/tok at ~270GB/s = ~10.6ms streaming; remaining ~36ms (77%) is per-token OVERHEAD (dispatch encode, barriers, bf16 casts, sync, argmax, 42-layer serialization over ~780 tiny dispatches). MLX 76 tok/s = 13.2ms/tok = ~10.6ms weight + ~2.6ms overhead.
implication: The gap vs MLX is per-token OVERHEAD, not GEMV efficiency. GEMV rewrite recovers ~1.3x max. Real levers: (1) cut dispatches/barriers/casts per token (per-layer or per-token megakernel / persistent-threadgroup decode); (2) block spec-decode (DFlash) amortizes overhead over K tokens per forward.
ship_now: MLX + DFlash: 20.5 mean / 32 (code) tok/s on 31B clears the >=15 gate today; custom engine 3.4-21 tok/s does not.
